_comment: DEMO, not the default: sensors that report something about themselves, not only a number.
Run it in the window (teleop on, so you drive the whole arena yourself). One command; the hall is
written below, because sats, quality zones and the dock are this hall's furniture.
ros2 launch mecanum_lab demo_sensor_reality.launch.py
Watch it from the outside (the readout line carries q, sats, degC and the lost count):
ros2 launch mecanum_lab lab.launch.py config:=config/demo_sensor_reality.json \
controller:=student/solution.py seconds:=30
Record it, and the same numbers land in the CSV that the lab report is written from. Grading is the
one-process command - grader, simulator and node on one clock, which is what the thresholds of
config/tasks.json are calibrated on (CONTRACT §9):
./lab grade --config config/demo_sensor_reality.json --task kinematik \
--controller student/solution.py --log messung.csv
Without ROS 2 the drive above is ./lab sim --config config/demo_sensor_reality.json, and the same
arguments --controller student/solution.py --seconds 30 go on ./lab run.
Why a file and not the default: the graded tasks in config/tasks.json are calibrated on the
clean sensors of each experiment. Every knob here is off in DEFAULT_CONFIG, and off means not
one random number is drawn that the old sensor did not draw - measured, see CONTRACT §6.4. A
demo asks for its imperfections; a graded run does not have them.
gps.dropout  = 0.15   probability per message that the transport loses it. The coin is tossed
before anything is measured, so the pattern of holes is the same for the
same --seed and has nothing to do with where the robot was. The readout
counts them (`lost 7`), the log writes them in `lost_gps`.
gps.latency  = 0.25   s on the wire, ±50 % jittered. A fix that is still travelling is not a
position that is wrong: it keeps the stamp it was measured with, so a
filter can see now - fix.t and predict over the gap. Measured over 25 s of
straight drive: a fix is 0.45 s old when it arrives (0.25 s of wire plus the
wait for the next emission slot), never older than 1.0 s. Watch `t_age_gps`.
gps.zones    = two rectangles, and they are here for `quality` and `sats`: 8 anchors on open
floor (quality 2), 3 between them and the pallet rack (quality 1), none
behind the loading-dock door (quality 0 = no fix, and the receiver then
sends nothing at all, which the readout shows as `q0 0 sats`).
imu.temp_*   = the chip warms 14 °C towards the temperature the drive current asks for, with
25 s of time constant, and the bias walks 3.5 mm/s² and 0.12 mrad/s per °C. That
is the drift a datasheet draws as a curve over temperature: it follows the load,
so it grows while the robot drives and walks back while it stands - and averaging
does not remove it, because it is an offset and not noise. `temp` itself is not a
field of sensor_msgs/Imu, so it is in the readout and in `temp_imu`, not on /imu.
lidar.reflectivity_min = 0.25  a beam only comes back if the wall returns at least a quarter
of what it got, which is |cos| of the incidence angle. Below it the beam
reports no echo (inf), so a long wall the robot drives alongside vanishes
in a wedge around the beam direction - why a real lidar does not see a
painted post you drive past. Measured 0.5 m off a 30 m wall: the wall is
seen 7.17 m down its length by default and 1.93 m here, 20 of 360 beams
come back with nothing. Counted in Scan.missing (`noecho_scan` column).
odom.jitter  = 0.35   each odom report reaches the bus up to 35 % of a period late, because that
is when an encoder report arrives. Never early and never out of order, so
only the stamps become uneven (20 ms ± 2.8 ms measured, mean and rate
unchanged); the values are integrated every physics step either way.
What a student does with it: drive the same line twice, once with this file and once without,
and compare `q_gps`, `lost_gps`, `temp_imu` and `noecho_scan` against the error of their own
filter. The conclusion is the exercise: a filter that treats every message as equally good is
a filter that is tuned for a sensor that does not exist.
_comment_view: This demo is about the measurements themselves — beams without echo, fixes with quality 1, a trail that drifts — so it asks for the layers the default view keeps empty.
_comment_tail: debug_truth publishes /<robot>/truth, so ghost, truth and GPS can be compared.
